questions.def: Mustn't expresses prohibition: you are not allowed to be late.
questions.question: You ___ be late for the meeting.

questions.def: Need to expresses necessity or obligation.
questions.question: I ___ go to the store today.

questions.def: Modal verbs like 'can' don't need 'to' after them.
questions.question: He can to speak three languages fluently.

questions.def: Can is used to ask for ability or possibility in present.
questions.question: ___ you help me with this?

questions.def: Could expresses past ability.
questions.question: She ___ play the piano when she was young.

questions.def: Should gives advice or recommendations.
questions.question: We ___ take an umbrella. It might rain.

questions.def: 'Mustn't' is a modal verb, so it doesn't need 'to'.
questions.question: You mustn't to eat so much sugar.

questions.def: 'May' asks for permission in a polite way.
questions.question: ___ I borrow your pen, please?

questions.def: 'Have to' expresses obligation.
questions.question: I ___ to study for the exam.

questions.def: 'Must' expresses a strong certainty or logical conclusion.
questions.question: He ___ be at work now. I saw him leave.

questions.def: Modal verbs (like 'should') are not followed by 'to'.
questions.question: She should to call her mother more often.

questions.def: Might indicates possibility, less certain than 'may'.
questions.question: It ___ rain later today.

questions.def: Mustn't is used to express strong prohibition.
questions.question: You ___ smoke in the hospital.

questions.def: Might expresses a possibility of being able to do something.
questions.question: I ___ be able to help you tomorrow.

questions.def: The correct form is 'You don't need to worry'.
questions.question: You need to worry. Everything will be okay.

questions.def: Don't need to expresses lack of necessity.
questions.question: You ___ buy milk. We have some.

questions.def: 'Would like' expresses a wish or desire.
questions.question: They ___ to go to the party, but they are busy.

questions.def: 'Can't have' expresses impossibility in the past.
questions.question: He ___ have taken the bus. I saw him walking.

questions.def: 'Must' is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: I must studied hard to pass the exam.

questions.def: Should have expresses a past regret or missed opportunity.
questions.question: We ___ have listened to your advice.

questions.def: Should is used to give advice.
questions.question: You ___ be quiet in the library.

questions.def: Have to expresses obligation or necessity.
questions.question: I ___ to finish this report by tomorrow.

questions.def: 'May' is a modal verb so it does not require 'to'.
questions.question: He may to come to the party.

questions.def: 'Could' makes a request more polite.
questions.question: ___ you please close the window?

questions.def: 'Can't have' indicates impossibility in the past.
questions.question: She ___ have gone to the store. I saw her at home.

questions.def: 'Shouldn't' is used to give advice or recommendations against something.
questions.question: You ___ eat so much junk food.

questions.def: 'Must' is a modal verb and is not followed by 'to'.
questions.question: They must to arrive on time tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Don't need' expresses lack of necessity.
questions.question: You ___ to water the plants today.

questions.def: Should is used to give advice
questions.question: I ___ study harder if I want to pass.

questions.def: Should expresses regret in the past using 'should have'.
questions.question: You ___ have told me you were coming!
